A1.justification: Both PDFs describe InkSight. Their main text, tables, equations, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original handwriting-conversion experiments, ablations, downstream recognition results, and a human evaluation on 200 HierText samples.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results in Section 4 and the corresponding appendices, including automated comparisons and human evaluation.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same frozen ViT and mT5 architecture, ink tokenization, five-task training mixture, greedy decoding, and word-segmented full-page inference. Expanded explanations do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: The public and proprietary training datasets, IAM/IMGUR5K/HierText evaluations, IAMOnDB recognition experiments, and full-page and sketch scenarios are retained. Newly disclosed proprietary dataset sizes describe existing coverage.

E2.justification: GVS remains the comparison method, with the same variant comparisons and binarized-input baseline choice. Human-traced controls and recognizers trained on real versus derendered ink are also retained.

E3.justification: The reported splits, filtering, model configurations, metrics, and training settings remain unchanged, including 340k training steps and batch size 512. The human study retains 200 samples, 16 evaluators, and three ratings per sample.

E4.justification: The inference-mode, augmentation, recognition-task, and frozen-encoder ablations are retained, alongside background-noise and erroneous-OCR examples. The 100-case open-ended-generation check also already appears in v1; v3 adds interpretation rather than another analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same three-initialization aggregates, uncertainty values, and stability curves using seeds 46, 64, and 2024. Human-evaluation agreement statistics are unchanged. Appendix G restates existing repeated-run information.

E6.justification: Benchmark scores, ablation values, human ratings, and qualitative outputs are unchanged; v1 Table 3's CER values 6.1, 7.8, and 4.6 become v3 Figure 9. However, v3 Appendix G newly reports approximate inference runtimes of one hour for a small model and three hours for Large-i across the three datasets.

T1.justification: The stroke representation, normalization, coordinate tokenization, and vocabulary-size expression 2N + 3 remain unchanged. Numbering the preprocessing steps adds explanation without changing mathematical definitions or reasoning.

C1.justification: v3 adds releasing Small-p weights, inference code, and generated and human-traced ink data to the introduction's contributions and conclusion. The central reading/writing-prior claims, generalization claims, and headline 87% and 67% findings remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 4.7 expands the existing segmentation limitation into explicit per-call length and complex-sketch restrictions. v3 also adds a background-noise hypothesis for recognition-task removal and interprets the retained generation failures as safeguards against forgery in Appendix N.3.

D1.justification: Where v1 describes release as ongoing, v3 provides explicit release links for code, weights, demo, and data, and describes InkML outputs. It adds dataset licenses, proprietary corpus sizes, and compute and inference-time disclosures. These substantially expand reproducibility documentation, although the recognizer citation is removed and the model card retains planned-release wording.

R1.justification: v3 removes the Carbune et al. (2020) recognizer citation and bibliography entry, replacing the citation with an anonymity footnote. Other research positioning and the trajectory-recovery survey remain substantially unchanged; PixelLLM's updated publication entry represents the same work.

P1.justification: v3 polishes prose, regroups contributions, enumerates normalization steps, adds a limitations subsection and appendix outline, moves impact statements to Appendix N, and removes acknowledgements. The principal method and evaluation narrative remains largely intact.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, with extensive resizing and relocation of displays. v1 Figure 5 is split into v3 Figures 5–6, the recognition-results table becomes a bar chart, human-evaluation plots are rearranged, and the dataset table gains a license column.

improvement.justification: v3 improves usability through explicit release/access information, fuller reproducibility documentation, clearer applicability limits, and more readable displays. The core empirical evidence is unchanged. Removing the recognizer citation and extending the unchanged 100-case generation check into broad anti-forgery claims temper these benefits, leaving a limited overall improvement.
